stands.title: wipeFoot's full-strength band stops at 0.26 cm but footClean grades out to 0.55 cm, so one tap of the sponge cannot pass the kiln's own foot gate on 6 of 8 forms
fix:
Make the sponge's full-strength band cover everything `footClean` grades, so the toast stops lying. One line, plus a shared constant.

In `src/sim/glazeField.js`, add near the top of the class file:
  `export const FOOT_CLEAN_H = 0.55;   // the band footClean() judges`

Then line 227 becomes:
  `const f = smoothstep(heightCm, Math.min(FOOT_CLEAN_H, heightCm * 0.9), this.mY[j]);`

and line 237 becomes `footClean(heightCm = FOOT_CLEAN_H) {` so the two can never drift apart again.

With the player's `wipeFoot(0.75)` this zeroes every graded cell at or below 0.55 cm and feathers 0.55 -> 0.75 so there is still a soft visual edge, not a razor line. `footClean` then reaches 1.000 on one tap for every form; `footRisk()` (line 368, band mY <= 0.32) is strictly inside the same band and is cleared too. The demo pot's `wipeFoot(0.6)` at `src/game/game.js:801` stays sane — the `Math.min` gives it a 0.54 -> 0.60 feather.

If keeping "some forms need two taps" is deliberate, the alternative minimal fix is to stop asserting success: make `src/game/game.js:2192-2195` read the field back and toast `'Foot wiped clean.'` only when `this.field.footClean() >= 0.45`, else something like `'Still glaze on the foot — go round it again.'` with class `''`. But the first fix is the one that matches the tool's stated contract at line 222.

One line, plus one shared constant so the two bands cannot drift apart again.

src/sim/glazeField.js:227 — the second smoothstep edge is a fraction of the WIPE height when it should be the height footClean actually grades:

  -      const f = smoothstep(heightCm, heightCm * 0.35, this.mY[j]);
  +      const f = smoothstep(heightCm, Math.min(FOOT_GRADE_CM, heightCm * 0.92), this.mY[j]);

  +export const FOOT_GRADE_CM = 0.55;   // the band footClean() grades; wipeFoot must clear all of it

stands.title: `mSide[j] > 1.5` is used to mean "the inside" but is also true for side 3, the base disc, so the sponge never touches the underside of the pot and nothing measures it
why:
STANDS — with one quoting slip in the original claim that does not touch the substance.

EXACT BYTES (awk NR-printed, not the Read tool):

  src/sim/glazeField.js:59    `    this.mSide = new Float32Array(GH);   // 0 outer, 1 rim, 2 inner, 3 base`
  src/sim/glazeField.js:105   `      this.mSide[j] = kk < 0.012 ? 3 : kk < 0.5 ? 0 : kk < 0.53 ? 1 : 2;`
  src/sim/glazeField.js:222   `  /** Wipe the foot — mandatory, or the pot welds to the shelf. */`
  src/sim/glazeField.js:225   `      if (this.mSide[j] > 1.5) continue;`
  src/sim/glazeField.js:240   `      if (this.mSide[j] > 1.5 || this.mY[j] > heightCm) continue;`   (footClean)
  src/sim/glazeField.js:371   `      if (this.mSide[j] > 1.5) continue;`                            (footRisk)

The claim's quote appended `   // spray does not reach inside` to line 225. That comment is real but lives on line 209, inside spray(), not on 225. The predicate itself — `this.mSide[j] > 1.5` used to mean "inside", while 3 = base also satisfies it — is verbatim at 225, 240 and 371.

MEASURED, not reasoned. I ran the repo's own harness (src/dev/realgame.mjs) on a stock jar (FORMS.jar, 18x12) and deleted the scratch probes afterward; `git status --porcelain src/` is clean.

  rows with mSide===3: 17 of GH=160  (10.6% of the meridian)
    mR 0.00 -> 4.12 cm at mY 0.000 -> 0.232 cm  — i.e. the entire flat underside

That is not a sliver. ProfileBuffer.build (src/render/potMesh.js:133-136) emits the base disc as only 3 of K=349 stations, but those 3 stations span the full base radius, and glazeField.bindProfile re-parameterises by ARC, so ~11% of the field rows land on them.

Rows each foot routine can still see after the `> 1.5` filter:
    wipeFoot(0.75):  2 rows
    footClean(0.55): 1 row
    footRisk(0.32):  0 rows
    rows excluded ONLY because mSide===3, with mY<=0.32:  17

Consequences, measured:
  - pour(0.25, 0.16, slot 0, 0.05, fromArc 0.5) x20 -> max glaze on base rows 0.7500.
    Three taps of wipeFoot(0.75) leave it at 0.7500. Unchanged. The sponge cannot touch it.
  - field.dip(1.0, 0, 0.14) (reachable: game.js:2172 calls dip(1 - clamp01(this._dipFrac)), and
    _dipFrac is clamp01(tool.y/height), so dragging the line to the foot gives 1.0)
    -> 0.2668 on the base; after wipeFoot still 0.2668.
  - footClean() after those pours + 3 wipes reports 0.683 — comfortably past the >= 0.40 gate at
    src/game/game.js:2898 — while the underside is at max thickness.
  - footRisk() = 0.000 after 21 pours. Base-inclusive it would be 0.750. Because zero rows survive
    `mSide<1.5 && mY<=0.32`, footRisk is identically 0 for this pot, so the weld check at
    src/game/game.js:2502 `if (this.fireResult && !this.fireResult.destroyed && footRisk > 0.30)`
    can never fire. The whole "welded to shelf" failure mode is dead code, and the base exclusion
    at line 371 is the direct cause.

And the game says this out loud. The wipe tool's own stage text, printed by the probe:
"Tap to sponge the foot clean. Do not skip this — glaze on the foot welds the pot to the shelf."

One precision the original claim got wrong by omission: line 209 (spray) should KEEP `> 1.5`.
A spray gun aimed at the side genuinely does not reach the underside, so excluding both inner and
base there is correct. The bug is at 225, 240 and 371 only. Line 257's `mSide[j] === 3` in stats()
is also deliberate and correct — the unglazable underside should not drag coverage down.

CONFIRMED — the mechanism is real, reachable, and it silently disables the game's own mandatory foot mechanic.

FACTS FROM THE CURRENT BYTES

src/sim/glazeField.js:105
      this.mSide[j] = kk < 0.012 ? 3 : kk < 0.5 ? 0 : kk < 0.53 ? 1 : 2;
with the legend on line 59: `0 outer, 1 rim, 2 inner, 3 base`. So `mSide[j] > 1.5` is true for BOTH 2 (inner) and 3 (base). Four sites use it:
  209  spray()     `if (this.mSide[j] > 1.5) continue;   // spray does not reach inside`
  225  wipeFoot()  `if (this.mSide[j] > 1.5) continue;`
  240  footClean() `if (this.mSide[j] > 1.5 || this.mY[j] > heightCm) continue;`
  371  footRisk()  `if (this.mSide[j] > 1.5) continue;`
The author clearly knew base is its own case — stats() at line 257 uses the exact test `if (this.mSide[j] === 3) continue;`.

(Minor correction to the candidate: the code it quoted is line 209, spray; the line it cited, 225, is wipeFoot. The substance is right; the quote was pasted from the wrong site.)

THE BASE IS NOT A ROUNDING ERROR. potMesh.js:135-137 builds a real base disc — put(0,0), put(r0*0.62,0), put(r0*0.985, ~0.045) — and GlazeField.bindProfile arc-length-parameterises it into GH=160 rows. Measured across all 8 FORMS x 3 masses: 11 to 23 of the 160 meridian rows are mSide===3. Demo jar (mass 1400, FORMS.jar): arcTotal 60.5 cm, rows j=0..18 are genuinely base (r 0 -> 6.85 cm at y 0.000-0.041), plus j=19 by the loose threshold.

GLAZE REALLY LANDS THERE. pour() (line 186) has no mSide guard at all and only skips `t > fromArc`, so every pour runs down the wall, over the foot and across the whole underside. dip() likewise: game.js:2172 calls `dip(1 - clamp01(this._dipFrac))`, and `_dipFrac = clamp01(this.tool.y / c.height)` (game.js:2086) hits 0 when the hand is at the wheel head, giving cut = 0 and coating the base.

REDONE ARITHMETIC — rows actually sampled (mSide <= 1.5 AND mY <= heightCm), out of 160:
  wipeFoot(0.75), as called from game.js:2181:  0 to 3 rows (24 of 24 configs <= 3; cup@2200 = 0)
  footClean(0.55):                              0 to 2 rows (5 of 24 configs = 0)
  footRisk(0.32), the destroy check:            0 rows in 18 of 24 configs
With the base counted instead of skipped, the same filters take 11-24 rows.

END-TO-END, real field, full dip then wipe:
  chawan  base carries 0.305 of glaze; wipeFoot(0.75) leaves it 0.305; footClean() = 1.000
  jar     base 0.305 before AND after wipe; footClean 0.000 -> 0.392; footRisk 0.000
  jar, pour instead of dip: base worst 0.443, unchanged by the wipe.
footRisk() returned exactly 0.000 for every form tested, with a third of a coat sitting on the shelf-contact face.

PLAYER-VISIBLE CONSEQUENCE, traced to the call sites:
  1. glazeField.js:223 documents the mechanic — "Wipe the foot - mandatory, or the pot welds to the shelf." The sponge provably never touches the underside, which is the entire surface that contacts the shelf (this pot has no foot ring; the base disc runs r=0 to r=r0 at y=0).
  2. game.js:2891 `if (gs.footClean < 0.4)` blocks firing with "The foot is still covered - it will weld to the shelf. Wipe it." On a chawan whose whole underside is glazed, footClean is 1.000 and the player is waved straight through.
  3. game.js:2501-2506 `const footRisk = this.field.footRisk(); if (... footRisk > 0.30) { destroyed; 'welded to shelf' }`. footRisk samples zero rows on most pots, so it returns 0 and this destruction branch is unreachable dead code.

So the whole weld-to-the-shelf system — a gate, a warning and a pot-destroying outcome — reads a one-to-two-row sliver of the outer wall at y ~ 0.45 cm, a surface that never touches the shelf, and is blind to the surface that does.

Three characters-worth of change, in three places. Exclude the INNER wall only, and let the base back in.

    -      if (this.mSide[j] > 1.5) continue;
    +      if (this.mSide[j] === 2) continue;        // inner wall only; the base is what sits on the shelf

  src/sim/glazeField.js:240  (footClean)
    -      if (this.mSide[j] > 1.5 || this.mY[j] > heightCm) continue;
    +      if (this.mSide[j] === 2 || this.mY[j] > heightCm) continue;

  src/sim/glazeField.js:371  (footRisk)
    -      if (this.mSide[j] > 1.5) continue;
    +      if (this.mSide[j] === 2) continue;

`put(0, Math.max(0.006, ymid(0) * 0.6), ...)` (src/render/potMesh.js:161) — the INSIDE floor of the
pot, mSide 2, mY ~0.006. It passes every `mY <= heightCm` test. Without an explicit side-2 guard,
wipeFoot would scrub the glaze off the inside of the pot's floor. The rim (side 1) needs no guard;
its mY is far above heightCm already.

that 0.30 if the wipe's smoothstep does not pull the base down far enough in one tap. Re-run
src/dev/_probe_wipe2.mjs and src/dev/_probe_rows.mjs, which already instrument exactly these numbers.

No perf concern: wipeFoot/footClean run on tap, footRisk once per firing, and stats() at 6 Hz — the
17 extra rows add 17*192 = 3,264 cell visits to a tap-frequency loop, nothing per-frame.

In C:/Users/oxman/everything/celadon/src/sim/glazeField.js, change the guard from "not outer" to "not inner" at the three foot sites, leaving spray alone:

stands.title: flow() sends the foot-ring row uphill during the firing, because it too reads side 3 as "inner"
why:
STANDS — and it is worse than "subtle": it can destroy the pot.

**The code is there, verbatim, at the claimed line.** `src/sim/glazeField.js:318-321`:

```
318:      const side = this.mSide[j];
319:      // on the inner surface "down" points the other way along the arc
320:      const inner = side > 1.5;
321:      const jTo = inner ? j + 1 : j - 1;
```

**Side 3 really is the foot, and `> 1.5` really does catch it.** `glazeField.js:59` documents `// 0 outer, 1 rim, 2 inner, 3 base`, and `:105` assigns `this.mSide[j] = kk < 0.012 ? 3 : ...` with `kk = k/K`, K=349 — so side 3 is profile stations k=0..4: the three base-disc points from `potMesh.js:134-136` (`put(0,0)`, `put(r0*0.62,0)`, `put(r0*0.985, ...)`) plus the first two outer-wall stations. `3 > 1.5` is true, so those rows take `jTo = j+1`. The codebase already knows 3 is not 2 — `stats()` at `:257` writes `if (this.mSide[j] === 3) continue;`.

**j+1 is demonstrably uphill there.** Building the game's own shapes (`Clay.sculpt` + `FORMS`/`targetSize` from `lore.js`, the same path `_footcheck4.mjs` uses) and reading mY/mDown directly: for a chawan, row j=22 is side 3 with `mDown = 0.864`, sits at y = 0.064 cm, and pushes to j=23 at y = 0.253 cm — climbing 1.9 mm — while its true downhill neighbour j=21 is at y = 0.022 cm. Across all 8 FORMS × 5 sizes, **40/40 have at least one side-3 row that passes the `down < 0.02` gate and flows uphill**, with `mDown` of 0.84–0.99 (cup 0.995, bottle 0.978, vase 0.935, urn 0.898, chawan 0.864, jar 0.842) — i.e. a near-vertical wall row at the foot running backwards at full Poiseuille rate, not a flat-base rounding artifact.

**Arithmetic.** flow() is not per-frame: `game.js:2392` steps it at 20 Hz (`_flowAcc >= 0.05`) across `dur = 40` s → 800 steps, those above 900 °C active. Per step `dtHours = (0.05/40) × scheduleHours × 0.55`; the default schedule gives scheduleHours = 20.92 h → 0.01438 h, `kFlow = dtHours*0.9 = 0.01294`. Each step the reversed row ships `min(kFlow·mob·down·h³·42, 0.42h)` — up to 42% of that row's glaze, 20 times a second, in the wrong direction.

**The player sees it, through two scored quantities.** `wipeFoot` (`:225`) itself skips `mSide > 1.5`, so the reversed row is precisely the one the mandatory foot wipe cannot reach; the firing then pumps that unwipeable glaze *up* into the band that `footRisk` (`:371`, y ≤ 0.32) and `footClean` (`:240`, y ≤ 0.55) do score. I replayed the real pipeline — `dip(1, 0, thickness)` → `wipeFoot(0.75)` → 800 steps at the shipped cadence — first checking my flow replica is byte-identical to the shipped `flow()` (max abs diff over the whole field after a full firing = 0). Of 300 configurations that pass the game's own kiln gate (`game.js:2898`, footClean ≥ 0.4), **22 flip the destroy verdict** at `game.js:2502` (`footRisk > 0.30` → "welded to shelf"):

- chawan, Zinc Flower, 0.8 mm coat, gate 0.73: current footRisk **0.302 → pot destroyed**; corrected 0.095. Post-fire footClean 0.000 vs 0.422.
- chawan, Raku, 0.8 mm, gate 0.73: 0.374 (destroyed) vs 0.092; footClean 0.000 vs 0.422.
- bowl, Raku, 0.8 mm, gate 0.69: 0.356 vs 0.130.
- plate, Zinc Flower, 1.2 mm, gate 0.50: 0.475 vs 0.244.

Even where it does not destroy the pot, footClean loses up to 0.42, which crosses the `scoring.js:120` threshold (`foot < 0.45` → "The foot was not wiped clean. That is how shelves get destroyed.") and costs 0.16 × 0.42 × 100 ≈ 6.7 points of surface score. So the player wipes the foot exactly as instructed, passes the gate, and the kiln tells them it welded to the shelf.

stands.title: snapshot() quantises the wax channel through the glaze-thickness scale, so a full wax resist comes back at 0.7 after a save and reload
why:
STANDS. The quoted line exists verbatim at src/sim/glazeField.js:445:

    for (let c = 0; c < 4; c++) out[q + c] = Math.round(clamp01(this.data[o + c] / 0.7) * 255);

Channel 3 is the wax mask (src/sim/glazeField.js:33 — `this.data = new Float32Array(GW * GH * 4);   // t0,t1,t2,wax`), and it is the one channel whose range is NOT 0..0.7. brush() caps it at 1.0 (src/sim/glazeField.js:146 — `this.data[o + 3] = Math.min(1, this.data[o + 3] + w * amount);`) whereas the three glaze channels clamp to 0.62 (brush), 0.7 (dip) and 0.75 (pour). The single 0.7 divisor is applied to all four.

Arithmetic, done by hand:
  encode  clamp01(1.0 / 0.7) = clamp01(1.4286) = 1.0 -> Math.round(1.0 * 255) = 255
  decode  src/sim/glazeField.js:465 — `this.data[o + c] = (bin.charCodeAt(q + c) / 255) * 0.7;`
          255 / 255 * 0.7 = 0.7
  loss    0.3 absolute, 30% of the channel.
Every wax value in [0.7, 1.0] maps to the same byte 255, so the top 30% of the wax range is discarded outright. Values below 0.7 round-trip fine at ~0.00275 resolution. clamp01 is `(v) => (v < 0 ? 0 : v > 1 ? 1 : v)` (src/core/util.js:8), so the clamp is what swallows the overflow silently.

Three things I checked that could each have refuted this:

1. Is wax still non-zero when snapshot() runs? Yes. The snapshot is taken post-firing at src/game/game.js:2579 (`field: this.field.snapshot()`), and flow() only iterates `for (let s = 0; s < SLOTS; s++)` i.e. channels 0..2 — it never touches +3. Line 146 is the ONLY write to `data[o + 3]` in the entire repo. So despite the HUD line at src/game/game.js:2363 ("Whatever was left of the wax and the organics is going up the chimney"), the mask is still sitting at 1.0 in the field when it is serialised.

2. Does the decode cancel the error? No — src/sim/glazeField.js:465 uses the same 0.7 scale, so the clip is permanent.

3. Is full saturation actually reachable in play? Yes, easily. src/game/game.js:2116 calls `this.field.brush(hAng, hit.arcT, GLAZE_TOOLS.wax.rad, slot, dt * 3.2, true)`. At 60fps dt = 0.0167, so amount = 0.0533 per frame; with w = 1 at the brush centre that is 1/0.0533 = 18.8 frames = ~0.31 s of holding to pin a cell at 1.0. Full-strength wax is the normal case, not an edge case.

Observable consequence — and this is why "subtle" is the correct severity, not worse. restore() is reached only from dressPot (src/game/piece.js:26, `game.field.restore(p.field)`), i.e. the shelf viewer for an already-fired piece. There dressPot sets `u.uFired.value = 1`, which makes the wax-appearance block dead: src/render/potMaterial.js:477-479 computes `float wv = wax * (1.0 - uFired);` = 0. The one live consumer is src/render/potMaterial.js:311:

    float cover = sstep(0.004, 0.045, gtot) * (1.0 - wax * 0.94);

  live pot     1.0 - 1.0*0.94  = 0.060
  reloaded     1.0 - 0.7*0.94  = 0.342
  ratio        5.7x more glaze coverage rendered inside the waxed area

That only reads as visibly wrong where glaze and wax overlap, because otherwise gtot is ~0 under the wax and sstep(0.004, 0.045, ~0) is ~0 regardless. Overlap does occur two ways: the wax brush only adds to +3 and never clears the glaze channels, so waxing over an already-glazed wall leaves gtot high under wax=1; and flow() ignores the wax mask entirely, so molten glaze runs down into waxed cells during the firing. In those regions a piece looks correctly bare on the wheel and comes back off the shelf with glaze bleeding through the resist.

Secondary, same line, same root cause (worth fixing in the same edit but not what the candidate claimed): pour() clamps to 0.75 (src/sim/glazeField.js:199) and flow() adds `tmp[o2 + s] += q * ratio` with no clamp at all, so pooled glaze can exceed 0.7 too — and 0.7..0.75+ all collapse to byte 255. The heavy run at the foot, which is the thing the player was watching, flattens to uniform 0.7 on the shelf.

Confirmed real, reachable, and visible. The line is verbatim at src/sim/glazeField.js:445. Channel 3 is wax (declared at :33 "t0,t1,t2,wax") and it is clamped to 1.0, not 0.7 — src/sim/glazeField.js:146: `this.data[o + 3] = Math.min(1, this.data[o + 3] + w * amount);` — while the glaze slots clamp to 0.62 (brush :149), 0.7 (dip :176), 0.5 (spray :216). So 0.7 is the glaze-thickness scale and wax is not on it.

Arithmetic, redone by hand: snapshot does clamp01(1.0 / 0.7) * 255 = clamp01(1.4286) * 255 = 255. restore (:465) does (255/255) * 0.7 = 0.7. Every wax value in [0.7, 1.0] saturates to byte 255 and returns as 0.7 — a 30% loss at full resist, and the whole plateau above 0.7 is flattened. Values below 0.7 round-trip fine, so the defect is purely a clip.

Reachable: the wax tool passes amount = dt * 3.2 (src/game/game.js:2116) and the kernel weight is w = 1 at brush center, so the center gains 3.2 * (1/60) = 0.0533 per frame at 60fps and hits the 1.0 clamp in ceil(1/0.0533) = 19 frames = 0.31 s of dwell. Saturation is the normal outcome for a tool whose stated job is "glaze will not stick where you paint this" — the player paints until it is solid. Nothing clears channel 3 before the save: flow() and wipeFoot() only write d[o+s] for s < SLOTS (SLOTS = 3, src/sim/glaze.js:21), and the only write to o+3 anywhere in the file is :146. Wax therefore survives the firing at full value into the snapshot.

Path traced end to end: src/game/game.js:2579 `field: this.field.snapshot()` into the gallery entry, persisted by SaveIO.save(s) two lines later; read back at src/game/piece.js:26 `game.field.restore(p.field)` inside dressPot(), which is called from showPiece() at src/game/game.js:2725 — and the comment at :2708 confirms the shelf is reachable from the pause menu.

Player-visible: src/render/potMaterial.js:213 `float wax = G.a;` then :311 `float cover = sstep(0.004, 0.045, gtot) * (1.0 - wax * 0.94);` and :453 `float mixAmt = cover; S.albedo = mix(S.albedo, glazeAlbedo, mixAmt);` (also rough, clear, metal, irid on the following lines). At wax = 1.0 the factor is 1 - 0.94 = 0.06; at wax = 0.7 it is 1 - 0.658 = 0.342. That is 5.7x more glaze blended over the bare clay in the resist area.  - "Make a card" -> showCard -> "Back" -> showPiece #2 -> line 2716 fires AGAIN and stashes S2 = the DRESSED state (fired/glazed/shelf body/shelf glaze field). S1 is discarded.

Slots are `[null,null,null]` during throw, so `applyFireResult(mat, null, ...)` (`potMaterial.js:714-720`) sets colA/colB/raw to grey 0.5 and zeroes P/Q/R/S. The contrast inside the same chain proves the mechanism rather than a typo: the neighbouring `.replace('#include <roughnessmap_fragment>', ...)`, `.replace('#include <emissivemap_fragment>', ...)` and `.replace('#include <normal_fragment_maps>', ...)` all DO land, because they target include *directives*, which are the only thing present at that stage. Reachable: src/game/game.js:107 `this.mat = createPotMaterial();`. Lit by direct lights, so RE_Direct_Physical actually executes — src/render/studio.js:984/1004/1016 are three DirectionalLights and :1025/:1066/:1071 are PointLights, with no `layers` filtering anywhere in src/render/studio.js. Nothing else in src/ touches THREE.ShaderChunk or defines a second onBeforeCompile (grep over src/ returns only potMaterial.js:114), so no other code supplies this shading.

Player-visible, redone arithmetic. Intended: dotNL = saturate((rawNL + 0.55) / 1.55^2) = saturate((rawNL + 0.55) / 2.4025). Actual (stock Lambert): dotNL = saturate(rawNL).
  rawNL = 1.00 -> intended 0.645 vs actual 1.000 (-35.5%)
  rawNL = 0.50 -> intended 0.437 vs actual 0.500
  rawNL = 0.00 (terminator) -> intended 0.229 vs actual 0.000
  rawNL = -0.30 -> intended 0.104 vs actual 0.000
  rawNL = -0.55 -> 0.000, both
So today the shadow side of the terminator on the pot receives literally zero direct irradiance and drops off in one hard step, which is the exact "hard surface" look the comment at :648-652 says it is there to remove. stands.title: Lifting one of three fingers slams the camera: goalRadius 58 -> 16, or 94 degrees of azimuth in one event
why:
Confirmed in the current bytes. touchGeometry() (src/game/game.js:288-296) destructures only the first two Map entries — `const [a, b] = pts;` (line 291) — in finger-landing order, so with 3+ fingers down it silently tracks the pair (A,B). onTouchUp (line 399) re-baselines the pinch state ONLY when the remaining count drops below two: `if (this._touches.size < 2) { this._pinch = null; this._pinchStart = null; this._gesture = null; ... }` (lines 402-405). Lift A or B out of three and size is still 2, so that block is skipped and `_pinch`, `_pinchStart` and `_gesture` all survive pointing at the old pair. The next pointermove (lines 348-350) does `const now = touchGeometry(); const was = this._pinch;` — `now` is the NEW pair (B,C), `was` is the OLD pair (A,B) — and feeds that pair-identity change into the camera as if it were hand motion.

Arithmetic, computed not eyeballed. Zoom path: line 385 `this.eng.rig.zoom(-dSpread * 3.2)` into engine.js:207 `goalRadius = clamp(goalRadius * (1 + dz*0.0014), this.minR, this.maxR)` gives factor = 1 - dSpread*0.00448. dSpread = 223.2 px zeroes the factor; anything beyond goes NEGATIVE and clamps to minR. Worked case, fingers A(300,400) B(360,420) C(700,500), lift A: pair(A,B) spread 63.2 -> pair(B,C) spread 349.3, dSpread 286.0, dz = -915.3, factor = -0.2815, 58 * -0.2815 = -16.32, clamp(...,16,150) = 16. That is goalRadius 58 -> 16 in a single event, and 58 is exactly CAMERA.radius (src/core/engine.js:50) with 16 exactly this.minR (src/core/engine.js:190). Orbit path: engine.js:201 `goalTheta -= dx * 0.0055`, so 94 deg = 1.6406 rad needs a 298.3 px centroid jump. Worked case A(120,400) B(180,400) C(900,400), lift A: cx 150 -> 540, dx 390, dTheta 2.145 rad = 122.9 deg in one event. The claimed 94 deg is not just reachable, it is exceeded on a 1024-px-wide iPad.

It fires even when the gesture had not yet been decided: the arbiter at lines 375-381 measures `now` against the stale `_pinchStart` (still the old pair), picks zoom or drag, and the branch at 384-394 applies the delta in that same event. Note the failure needs the lifted finger to be one of the first two that landed (2 of the 3 cases); lifting the third finger leaves pair (A,B) intact and is harmless. Nothing else clears the state on this path — the `up` handler at line 441 sees `wasMulti` true and returns straight after onTouchUp, and only window blur (line 462) clears `_touches`.

At 60fps this is not a per-frame accumulation; it is one discrete event that pins the radius at the minimum or swings azimuth past 90 degrees, followed by the rig damping (engine.js:228-231, k=5.2) racing to the new goal over roughly a fifth of a second. Visible-wrong is the right severity.

stands.title: The wheel-speed assist overwrites omegaTarget every frame, so the pedal, the scroll wheel and W/S all decay back within a second
why: Confirmed against current bytes. src/game/game.js:1437-1439 runs every frame: 1437: if (assist && tId === 'hands') { 1438: const want = clamp(40 / Math.max(4.2, c.maxR), 3.0, 8.6); 1439: this.setWheelSpeed(damp(this.omegaTarget, want, 2.2, dt)); REACHABLE BY DEFAULT. src/game/save.js:61 ships `assist: true`, and game.js:1394 reads `const assist = this.save.settings.assist !== false;`. game.js:1224 sets `this.toolId = 'hands'` on entering the throw, and _updateThrow is dispatched every frame from update() at game.js:1309-1310 (`case ST.THROW: this._updateThrow(dt); break;`). The block has no gate on `pressing` or on any override flag. `grep -n "_toldWheel|_wheelManual|manual|override|_wheelUser|_userWheel|_wheelTouched" src/game/game.js` returns only lines 1440-1441, which are the one-shot toast latch — there is no manual-override state anywhere in the file. ALL THREE CONTROLS WRITE THE SAME FIELD. Scroll: game.js:478 `this.setWheelSpeed(this.omegaTarget - Math.sign(e.deltaY) * 1.15);`. Keys: game.js:542-543 `± 1.6`. Pedal: src/ui/hud.js:110 `this.game.setWheelSpeedFrac?.(f)` -> game.js:551-552, bound only to pointerdown/pointermove (hud.js:114-118), so it stops writing the moment the finger stops moving. All funnel into setWheelSpeed (game.js:546-548), which only assigns this.omegaTarget. ARITHMETIC, REDONE. damp is `lerp(a, b, 1 - Math.exp(-lambda*dt))` (src/core/util.js:23). With lambda = 2.2: - per frame @60fps: 1 - e^(-2.2/60) = 1 - 0.96401 = 0.03599 -> 3.60% of any manual offset erased EVERY FRAME - per second: e^(-2.2) = 0.1108 -> 88.9% of the offset gone in 1.0 s; 99% gone by 2.1 s The visible wheel is worse than a plain decay because omega chases a retreating target (game.js:1287-1288, spin-up rate 2.4). Solving y' = 2.4(x - y) with x = D*e^(-2.2t) gives y = 12*D*(e^(-2.2t) - e^(-2.4t)), which peaks at t = ln(2.4/2.2)/0.2 = 0.435 s at y = 0.384*D. So: - one W press (D = 1.6 rad/s, nominally +15.3 rpm) moves the actual wheel by only 0.61 rad/s ~ 5.9 rpm, then fades out - pedal dragged to full: MAX_RPM = 190 (game.js:29) -> 19.90 rad/s target, but `want` is clamped to <= 8.6 rad/s (82 rpm), so D = 11.3. The gauge climbs to ~124 rpm and slides back to ~82 rpm. The top ~57% of the pedal's travel is unreachable for more than ~1.5 s while hands is the tool. THE PLAYER SEES IT. The RPM gauge is driven from omega (game.js:1609-1610, `const rpm = (this.omega * 60) / TAU;`), and the pedal IS that gauge (src/ui/hud.js:103-105 adds class 'pedal' to `.gauge[data-g="rpm"]`), so the bar visibly crawls back out from under the finger that just set it. And game.js:1442 promises the opposite in words: 'The wheel finds its own speed, slowing as the pot opens out. W and S to take it over.' Nothing in the code ever lets W/S take it over. One correction to the claim's wording: omegaTarget loses 89% of a manual offset within 1.0 s, but the visible omega, having peaked at only 38% of the intended step at t ~ 0.44 s, takes about 2 s to fully settle back. That makes the claim slightly optimistic about the timing, not wrong about the defect.

stands.title: The two-finger banding-wheel flick uses a magic *22 where the mouse path divides by real elapsed time
why:
CONFIRMED, present verbatim right now.

src/game/game.js:390 (two-finger touch drag, glaze room):
    this._bandV = clamp(dx * BAND_RAD_PER_PX * 22, -BAND_MAX, BAND_MAX);

src/game/game.js:259-263 (the mouse right-drag, same quantity computed correctly):
    const now = performance.now();
    const gap = Math.max(1, now - (this._bandT ?? now));
    this._bandT = now;
    const v = dx * BAND_RAD_PER_PX / (gap / 1000);
    this._bandV = clamp((this._bandV ?? 0) * 0.6 + v * 0.4, -BAND_MAX, BAND_MAX);

UNITS. _bandV is radians per SECOND. Proof in the file, not inference: line 409 (touch release) and line 450 (mouse release) both do `this._band = Math.abs(this._bandV ?? 0) > 0.35 ? this._bandV : 0`, and line 2039-2041 says "`_band` is radians per SECOND, so this behaves the same at 30 fps and at 144" then integrates `this.pot.rotation.y += this._band * dt`. At line 390 `dx * BAND_RAD_PER_PX` is radians PER EVENT. Multiplying by 22 converts per-event to per-second only if events arrive every 1000/22 = 45.45 ms, i.e. at 22 Hz. Safari on iPad dispatches pointermove at the display refresh: 16.67 ms (60 Hz) on a standard iPad, 8.33 ms (120 Hz) on a ProMotion iPad Pro/Air. Neither is 22 Hz.

TWO COMPOUNDING ERRORS, and the second is why a naive fix is also wrong.
(1) Wrong constant. The true factor is the event rate, 60 or 120, not 22.
(2) Pointer events are per-finger. `dx = now.cx - was.cx` (line 353) is the delta of the two-finger MIDPOINT, and `this._pinch = now` (line 350) refreshes the reference on EVERY event. In a frame where both fingers travel D, two events fire and each moves cx by only D/2. So per-event dx is HALF the per-frame midpoint travel. (The accumulation at line 389 is fine — D/2 + D/2 = D — it is only the instantaneous velocity that is halved.)

ARITHMETIC, a flick where both fingers travel 800 px/s.
Intended: 800 * 0.007 = 5.6 rad/s, clamped by BAND_MAX to 3.2 (line 35).
60 Hz iPad: midpoint moves 13.33 px/frame, delivered as two events of 6.67 px. Line 390 gives 6.67 * 0.007 * 22 = 1.03 rad/s. 3.1x short of the 3.2 clamp.
120 Hz iPad Pro: 6.67 px/frame, two events of 3.33 px. 3.33 * 0.007 * 22 = 0.51 rad/s. 6.3x short, and only 0.16 above the 0.35 rad/s throw threshold at line 409 — so on that hardware most flicks are discarded outright and the wheel just stops dead.
Coast angle, integrating the decay at line 2042 (exp(-2.2t)), total = v/2.2 rad:
  3.2 rad/s -> 1.45 rad = 83 deg, about a quarter turn (what a banding wheel should do)
  1.03 rad/s -> 0.47 rad = 27 deg
  0.51 rad/s -> 0.23 rad = 13 deg, i.e. nothing
Same hand, same flick, and the result differs 2x between two iPads purely on refresh rate. That is the actual defect: the throw is a function of the device's event cadence, not of how fast the player moved.

Third, smaller: line 390 has no smoothing at all. The mouse path EMAs 0.6/0.4 over the last few events (line 263) so the throw is "the speed of the throw and not of the whole drag"; the touch path uses the single last event, so one small trailing sample as the fingers settle zeroes the flick.

Not previously fixed — nothing in the already-fixed list touches BAND_*, _bandV, or onTouchMove's drag branch.

The claim stands and I traced it end to end on the current bytes.

THE TWO PATHS
src/game/game.js:255-263 (mouse, right-drag):
  this.pot.rotation.y += dx * BAND_RAD_PER_PX;
  const now = performance.now();
  const gap = Math.max(1, now - (this._bandT ?? now));
  this._bandT = now;
  const v = dx * BAND_RAD_PER_PX / (gap / 1000);
  this._bandV = clamp((this._bandV ?? 0) * 0.6 + v * 0.4, -BAND_MAX, BAND_MAX);

src/game/game.js:388-390 (two-finger):
  this.pot.rotation.y += dx * BAND_RAD_PER_PX;
  this._bandV = clamp(dx * BAND_RAD_PER_PX * 22, -BAND_MAX, BAND_MAX);

Constants: BAND_RAD_PER_PX = 0.007 (line 33), BAND_MAX = 3.2 (line 35).

REACHABLE
- game.js:336 sets `this.pointer.right = true` when the second finger lands (onTouchDown, size === 2), and onTouchDown returns true so pointerdown returns early.
- game.js:376-381 decides the gesture once: `this._gesture = spreadBy > carriedBy ? 'zoom' : 'drag'` after 14 px. A sideways two-finger drag gives carry > spread, so 'drag'.
- game.js:386-390 is the `_gesture === 'drag'` + `state === ST.GLAZE` branch. Plain two-finger sideways drag in the glaze room.
- game.js:406-410 on lift: `if (this.pointer.right) { ... this._band = Math.abs(this._bandV ?? 0) > 0.35 ? this._bandV : 0; }`
- game.js:2040-2043 integrates it: `rotation.y += this._band * dt; this._band *= Math.exp(-2.2 * dt)`.
No early return or GLAZE-specific block anywhere on that chain. Also confirmed no double-application: pointermove line 227-229 returns as soon as onTouchMove returns true (size >= 2), so the mouse branch at 230 never runs for the two-finger case.

THE ARITHMETIC, REDONE
Pointer Events deliver one pointermove per finger, and onTouchMove (game.js:345) writes only `e.pointerId` into `this._touches` before recomputing geometry. So in any single event only one of the two points has moved, and `dx = now.cx - was.cx` is HALF that finger's step.

With both fingers travelling at midpoint speed v px/s and a per-finger event rate R:
  per-event dx = v / (2R)
  _bandV = dx * 0.007 * 22 = v * 0.007 * (11 / R)
True angular velocity is v * 0.007. So the code is correct only when R = 11 Hz. iPad Safari fires pointermove at display rate: 60 Hz, or 120 Hz on a ProMotion iPad. The multiplier that belongs there is 2R = 120 or 240, not 22 — short by 5.5x at 60 Hz and 10.9x at 120 Hz. (Degenerate case where one finger pivots around a planted thumb: still short by 22/R, i.e. 2.7x at 60 Hz, 5.5x at 120 Hz. Every finger pattern is too weak.)

PLAYER-VISIBLE
Coast angle is v0/2.2 rad, gated at |v0| > 0.35 and capped by BAND_MAX = 3.2:
  midpoint 400 px/s  -> mouse 73 deg | touch@60 13 deg | touch@120 0 deg (0.26 rad/s, below the 0.35 gate)
  midpoint 500 px/s  -> mouse 83 deg | touch@60 17 deg | touch@120 0 deg (0.32 rad/s, below the gate)
  midpoint 800 px/s  -> mouse 83 deg | touch@60 27 deg | touch@120 13 deg
  midpoint 2000 px/s -> mouse 83 deg | touch@60 67 deg | touch@120 33 deg
On a ProMotion iPad — the stated primary device — any flick under roughly 550 px/s of midpoint travel yields no coast at all, while the identical gesture on a mouse saturates BAND_MAX and coasts the full 83 deg. Even a hard 2000 px/s flick gets 33 deg instead of 83 deg. The banding wheel is the glaze room's core affordance (comment at line 240-241: "a flick at the end lets it coast — which is what a banding wheel does"), so on the iPad the wheel effectively does not coast. Real, reachable, and felt.

refuted.title: The one-column glaze shelf rule is dead: a later three-column rule wins on narrow AND short windows

why:
The mechanism exists but the consequence does not, and the description of what gets blurred is wrong.

FACTS (real bytes):
- src/sim/clay.js:1070 `blur1(this.m, 2, 1, this._tmp);` — inside `if (isWet)` (line 1063).
- src/sim/clay.js:1166-1167 `blur1(this.ox, 2, 1, t2);` / `blur1(this.oz, 2, 1, t2);` — inside `if (isWet && omega > 0.4)` (line 1150).

step() never blurs ri/ro. The silhouette is only smoothed via `_blurAbove(arr, from, radius, amount)` (line 973), which already takes a dt-scaled amount (`this._smoothProfile(1, 0, clamp01(dt * 14))`, line 803) and was clearly fixed for exactly this reason. The three step() blurs touch moisture and the lean offsets only.

ARITHMETIC. 5-tap box transfer function H(k) = (1 + 2cos k + 2cos 2k)/5, NS = 168 (line 28). The seeded wobble (lines 154-156) is `sin(ph + t*2.1)`, i.e. k = 2.1/168 = 0.0125 rad/section, so H = 0.99984 per frame -> 0.94%/s decay at 60 Hz, 1.87%/s at 120. Twice the rate, of ~1% per second.

- Passive wet spin at omega 20 for 60 s: metrics().wobble 0.13511 @60 Hz vs 0.13485 @120 Hz (0.2%); trueness 0.782 vs 0.783. Kill threshold is 1.9 (line 1215); "centered" flips at trueness > 0.86 (line 394).
- Realistic thrown pot (center 3 s, open 3 s, pull 5 s, 2 s of unsteady-hand nudges): the ox field's high-frequency energy fraction is 4.1e-5 — a radius-2 box has almost nothing to remove. Blurring that field alone for a further 10 s: wobble 0.02104 @60 Hz vs 0.01985 @120 Hz. That is 0.0012 on a scale whose trueness denominator is 0.62.
- Moisture: the blur conserves the mean exactly (0.6556 vs 0.6556 to 4 dp), so metrics().moisture — the number the HUD and scoring read — is frame-rate identical. Only the local peak differs: after 2 s of sponging then 3 s of spinning, peak m 0.7816 @60 vs 0.7474 @120; yieldStrength at that section 116782 vs 118095 (1.1%); plasticity 1.0 in both. Worst case is the first second after heavy sponging, where plasticity at the single wettest section reads 0.854 vs 0.930 — one section, one factor among five inside a clamp01, for about a second.

Cost is also a non-issue: 3 x 168 x 5 = 2520 reads/frame.

So: reachable (throwing screen, wheel on), arithmetic holds in the log sense, and invisible to the player in every metric the game surfaces or kills on. Refuted on magnitude.

(Adjacent, and NOT this claim, so I did not carry it to a conclusion: the slump caps in the same loop — `Math.min(rate * 0.30 * w, 0.018)` at line 1099 and `Math.min(rate * 0.9 * w, 0.004)` at line 1128 — are per-FRAME ceilings on a dt-scaled rate, so once over-stress is high enough for the cap to bind, the lean grows at 0.24 cm/s at 60 Hz and 0.48 cm/s at 120. The MECHANISM is exactly as claimed, but the CONSEQUENCE ("blurs the bore outright") fails both the arithmetic and end-to-end measurement.

WHAT IS TRUE
- src/sim/clay.js:432 `    this._blurAbove(this.ri, lowest, 2);` — genuinely the only one of the five call sites that omits `amount`. The others all forward it: 885/886 (`this._blurAbove(mid, from, radius, amount)` / `th`), 930/931 (`this._blurAbove(this.ro, from, radius, amount)` / `this.ri`).
- Signature at :973 `_blurAbove(arr, from, radius = 1, amount = 1)`, and :993 `if (amount >= 1) { for (let i = lo; i < NS; i++) arr[i] = t[i]; return; }` — so line 432 does take the full-replacement branch, not the rate branch.
- Reachable once per RENDERED frame, no substepping: main.js:170 `const dt = Math.min(0.05, (now - last) / 1000);` in a plain rAF loop -> game.js:1452 `this.hand.apply(c, {...}, dt)` -> hand.js:137 `c.open(...)`. It does not depend on `work`/dt at all, so a parked finger fires it too.

WHY IT IS NOT THE REPORTED DEFECT
Arithmetic: NS = 168 (clay.js:28) and the kernel is radius 2 — a 5-tap box on a 168-section grid. Its per-pass variance is (5^2-1)/12 = 2, i.e. D = 1 section^2/frame, so information spreads sqrt(2n) sections in n frames: ~11 of 168 after 1 s at 60 fps, ~19 after 3 s. That is ~6% of the profile per second, not an outright blur. Measured on the isolated array, low-frequency bore amplitude decays only 32% in a full second (1.4597 -> 0.9879) and needs ~1800 frames (30 s of continuous pressing) to flatten to 0.054.

Measured end to end (real clay.js vs a copy patched to `clamp01(dt*20)`, identical 3 s centre + 6 s open, seed 11, 1250 g):
- height 9.14 vs 9.15 cm; diameter 11.08 vs 11.06 cm; rim bore 2.014 vs 2.012; max bore 2.0157 vs 2.0159.
- wallEven 0.8967 vs 0.8972 after opening, 0.7957 vs 0.7960 after three pulls. Via scoring.js:102 (`0.30 * even`) that is 23.87 vs 23.88 — 0.01 of a 100-point craft score.
- The whole difference sits in ~20 sections at the inside corner where floor meets wall (y ~ 1.0-2.4 cm): ri[18] = 1.258 (real) vs 0.880 (patched). Above y ~ 4 cm the two profiles agree to 0.006 cm. Rounding that inside corner is what a thrown pot actually has, so it is not even clearly wrong.
- Frame-rate spread is real but tiny: 120 Hz vs 60 Hz on the real code gives ri[18] = 1.416 vs 1.258 (0.16 cm at one height near the floor), wallEven 0.8956 vs 0.8967, height and diameter identical to 2 dp.

- No floor damage: `lowest` guards it (floorSection() = 14 in both builds), and a 5 s resting hand actually widens the bore (+37.7% span), so there is no runaway.

The player cannot see 0.16 cm of inside-corner radius that the next stroke overwrites, and it moves the grade by 0.01 points. Real smell, not a real bug.
